v1_coach_answers_applied.change: Every exercise is tagged on all lenses at once: family, pattern, laterality, plane, size class, main muscles, equipment and level, plus the v1 fields below. The record schema (8.3) marks these tags as required, so the generator can segment the library by any of them.

Size classes are now the coach's rule. BIG = quads, glutes, hamstrings, lats/upper back, chest. SMALL = biceps, triceps, side delts, rear delts, calves, forearms, abs. Front delts, traps, adductors and neck are still unclassified (PROPOSED placements, pending).

Biomechanics is the description every exercise carries (plane, laterality, load position, stance, ROM, zone), not a bucket of exercises. The FN family is renamed 'Functional systems (carries, drags, slings)'.

Exercise level = skill + stability demand + load position (in front / low -> on the body -> behind the body or overhead), read through Pat Davidson's zones; machines and cables lower it. New facet F.DZONE: Z1 vertical-low (arms down, standing), Z2 horizontal (hands in front, knee at hip height), Z3 vertical-high (arms overhead, deep squat). Z1 and Z3 carry an external-rotation bias; Z2 carries an internal-rotation bias and is compressive. F.LOADPOS values get level bands, and the RP.KD.BS level driver is rewritten (goblet / zercher L1, front squat L2, back squat L3).
Levels add options and never remove them, and they are still theoretical. The generator uses exercise level and client level as soft defaults (ordering, suggestions), never as a gate.

Client level and exercise level stay separate (confirmed). Client levels are renamed Level 1 / 2 / 3; NOVICE and NEWBY describe the same kind of client (under about 6-12 months of training, or back after more than 6-12 months off).
The BYOP 'MASTER EXERCISE LIBRARY' is the single source of truth. Sheet23 and RESISTANCE PATTERNS are older drafts, used only for levels and the exercise grammar.

Core rule confirmed: CO.CT = the trunk moves on a still pelvis, CO.CP = the pelvis/legs move on a still trunk, CO.CB = both at once, each in any plane (static or dynamic). CO.CB is now a confirmed region. Toes to bar and the Copenhagen plank are 'more complicated' (PROPOSED homes, pending).

New LEG FLEXION node RP.LF (knee flexion: leg curls, Nordics, slider / ball curls), separate from hip dominant and organised like bicep curls. It replaces RP.HD.ISO (retired id, kept as an alias) and counts toward hamstrings, never toward the hinge pattern. Lanes RP.LF.MACH and RP.LF.BW are PROPOSED.

The Sheet23 plyo 'ZONE 1/2/3' is not a zone. Facet F.PZONE is replaced by F.PMETHOD, a neutral 'plyo execution method' axis: receive and pause -> receive then create -> repeated receive/create, mapped to the four force phases. The coach has not named it yet. Unilateral plyos are harder than bilateral, and programs start with more receiving.

F.ZONE_SENSES rewritten. ZONE_ARM becomes ZONE_DAVIDSON (the cable curl / triceps 'Zone 1/2/3' are Davidson arm-position zones); ZONE_PLYO points to F.PMETHOD; ZONE_BAND (Sheet23 column A) is re-read as Davidson zones used as a level band (INFERRED).

The coach did not understand the 'grammar' question, so the base + variables grammar (8.3-8.4) stays a team proposal, to be re-asked in plain words. PER-02 (RIGHT) does confirm how it is used: exercises stay fixed for a 4-6 week block, and the next block changes one or two of grip, stance, implement, range of motion or rep range, never all at once.

F.LOADLAT rewritten in the coach's words: a contralateral load pulls you INTO the hip, an ipsilateral load helps you OUT of it. Use cases: change-of-direction sports (football route runners, soccer, basketball, tennis); sprint acceleration (ipsilateral step-ups); bodybuilders and powerlifters as a health accessory, mostly in the first 2-4 weeks. The v0 'contralateral is the default' assumption is retired.

Ballistic vs plyometric is defined by ground-contact time: longer on the ground = ballistic, shorter = plyometric. The sport's own ground-contact time sets the ratio, and programs start ballistic and become more plyometric. F.INTENT and the sport-dial table (4.6) are updated.

No bands and no variable resistance. F.ACCOM becomes a DORMANT future axis that the generator does not use; the BAND implement is dormant; every banded, reverse-banded or chained item is out of scope; F.PERTURB=HIP_BAND is dormant; the banded worked example is rewritten.

F.PERTURB=STRAP removed ('strap rotating in/out' taken away). 'Camporini Deadlifts' removed. 'Pull under' = lat pull-over (RP.PL.V.ISO renamed). 'Kong Rows', 'Low DB Squats', 'Single Leg Get Ups' and 'Alternating DB/Barbell Deadlifts' are described and placed (6.2).
Throws and GHD have no levels (L0). The two GHD entries (AN48 MODERATE, AN93 ADVANCED) become one record.
The '-ADVANCED' label on leg extensions (AM3) and the 'UNILATERAL' label on leg curls (AR5) are typos: both are available at every level.
Dips are credited 0.5 triceps / 0.5 chest and programmed on push days. Upright rows stay side-delt work.
Near-duplicates merged: 'Side Plank ' (thorax) + 'Side Planks ' (pelvis) become one record (PROPOSED CO.CB, frontal, static); the seated DB curl entries AS14 / AS16 become one record.

The default helper credit is 0.25 (was 0.5) in every node and in the slot table. Horizontal and mid-range pushing credit chest 1.0 with front delts and triceps as helpers at 0.25, as in the coach's own VOL-09 example (bench: chest main mover, triceps and front delts helpers); the row-6 label 'CHEST/FRONT DELTS' no longer gives front delts 1.0. Unilateral knee dominant = quads 1.0, glutes 0.25. Hinges = hamstrings 1.0, glutes 0.5 (PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL, the volume engine's value; the v0 glutes 1.0 is retired). Thrusters = quads 1.0 + front delts ('shoulders') 0.5: the thruster-specific answer LIB-14 (RIGHT) governs over the general helper rule, the same choice as 12_volume_algorithm_v1.md.
Athletic patterns (jumps, throws, Olympic lifts, sprints, COD) never count toward muscle volume: every AP default muscle credit is emptied, and ankle hops in calf slots are not calf sets.

Muscle size no longer picks the weekly 3/5/7 % ramp (the person's state does). Size class still sets the organising lens and the default rep range (small 12-30, big 5-15 mixed). 40-rep sets only as a CrossFit / AMRAP option.

F.CONSTRAINT uses the approved 1-5 scale. Machines are not ranked by preference: hack squat and leg press are more constrained than the Smith machine, the belt squat avoids axial load, GHD / reverse hyper only if available and felt in the right muscles. Safety beats the level label for older and injured clients.
New facet F.AXIAL (axial spinal load HIGH / LOW / NONE), so the generator can load the spine heavily once a week (squat; deadlifts also count) and use leg press or belt squat for the second exposure.

Full lifts renamed Squat Snatch / Squat Clean / Squat Clean & Jerk; 'Weighted squat to calf raise' takes any implement. Push press is the easier rung, push jerk intermediate/advanced. Everyone in athletic training gets Olympic lifts (beginners: DB/KB snatches and cleans, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls and hang cleans); youth may lift from the floor.

coach_statements_in_brief: Different athletes need different things: basketball more plyos; boxers and karate fewer; MMA more than boxers but less than basketball; play with the volume.
Some need more resistance training, some more power/explosiveness with athletic patterns.
The hardest thing is the categorization: bigger muscles, smaller muscles, biomechanics; (changing) athletic patterns, resistance patterns, core.
Mix of Dr. Pat Davidson, Dr. Mike Israetel and first-principles training science - not somebody's packaged model (5-3-1, Texas Method, Prilepin).

15-20 sets per muscle per week; more for a muscle to grow, fewer with injury/pain; ramp 3/5/7% per week by muscle size [SUPERSEDED by COACH-ANSWER VOL-05: the rate follows the person's state, not muscle size; 15-20 refined by VOL-01 - see coach_statements_superseded]; smaller muscles take more reps; everyone picks 5-30 reps.

how_they_intersect: Lens B picks the FAMILY (row 4: ATHLETIC / RESISTANCE / CONTROL, plus CARDIO and FUNCTIONAL) = what quality a slot trains and how it is dosed.

Lens A's size cut (bigger / smaller muscles, COACH-ANSWER CAT-02) picks how the library LIST is organised inside RESISTANCE: big muscles by pattern (joint dominance x laterality, push/pull x vector), small muscles by muscle (one unlevelled list each).
'Biomechanics' is not a third bucket (COACH-ANSWER CAT-03): it is the description every exercise carries - plane, laterality, load position, stance, ROM, Davidson zone - in every family.

Athletic patterns and core are also organised by pattern (force phase, start position, turn angle, plane, region), never by muscle; their PURPOSE row names a quality ('SPEED/POWER', 'CHANGE OF DIRECTION', 'CORE') and athletic work never counts toward muscle volume (VOL-10).
The program slot is the intersection: PURPOSE (muscle credited, Israetel lens) x CATEGORY (pattern bucket, Davidson lens).

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Two names for one level system, plus five meanings of 'ZONE'
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: Level words EASY/FOUNDATIONAL/FOUNDATINONAL, MODERATE/INTERMEDIATE/INTERMIDIATE, ADVANCED/HARD, ANY; 'ZONE' = level row (A3), plyo execution zone (Sheet23 C34:D36), arm-position zone (AS12), unexplained colour band (Sheet23 A2:A28), energy zones (BASEBALL / AEROBIC).
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: A generator reading 'ZONE 2' or 'MODERATE' cannot know which axis is meant.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: One level field (L0-L3); separate fields F.PMETHOD (plyo execution method), F.DZONE (Davidson position zone), F.ABAND (aerobic band), F.EZONE (energy zone).
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Resolved (COACH-ANSWER CAT-04, CAT-10, CAT-11): Davidson zones -> F.DZONE; plyo 'zones' -> F.PMETHOD (not a zone); ZONE_BAND read as Davidson-zone level band (INFERRED).

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Exercise tier vs client level are conflated in vocabulary but independent in practice
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: NOVICE/NEWBY/INTERMEDIATE change dose only in UL and almost only in PPL (one swap: NOVICE 'Cable Lat pulldown' C28 vs 'Pull ups or Cable Lat pull down' G28/K28); NOVICE gets 'Sqats or Leg Press' and 'Deadlifts (DB or Barbell)' although BYOP files leg press and barbell deadlifts ADVANCED and DB deadlifts MODERATE; JUSTICE LEAGUE mixes FOUNDATIONAL plyos with an ADVANCED power clean; the 'NOVICE' column sits below the 'NEWBY' column (column order only: the coach uses both words for a beginner, PRG-05).
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: If 'level' is one field the generator will lock beginners out of good tools (leg press) and lock advanced athletes out of foundational landings.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Two fields: F.LEVEL (exercise) and F.CLIENT (person). Client level caps per-node tier, not globally.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Resolved (COACH-ANSWER CAT-06, PRG-05): two separate fields; client levels named Level 1/2/3 by column position (NOVICE column = Level 1, NEWBY = Level 2, INTERMEDIATE = Level 3); as words, novice and newbie mean the same kind of beginner.

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Level means different things per bucket and is missing where it matters
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: TEX = complexity/start position; JMP = height/base/load; COD = turn angle; core = plane; upper RP = remove external support; lower RP = load position then methods/machines; UL lanes and all isolation lists unlevelled; VERTICAL PULL / VERTICAL PUSH / HORIZONTAL PULL have no INTERMEDIATE; AQ is labelled FOUNDATIONAL as a whole.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: A single 'difficulty' number is meaningless across buckets.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Keep tiers but store the 'level_driver' per node (in the JSON) and let UL/ISO derive difficulty from facets (load position, stance, load laterality).
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Addressed (COACH-ANSWER CAT-04): one definition - skill + stability + load position / Davidson zone, machines easier; per-bucket drivers stay. CAT-05: levels are theoretical, soft defaults only.

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Mixed lists: isolation, ballistic and other-pattern items live inside compound columns
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: Leg extension in all 3 AI blocks; 9 of 33 AN options are knee-flexion curls; flies in AD; push press/jerk and thrusters in AA; thrusters again in AI; KB face pulls in U; front raises and reverse flies in the 'ABdution' list; upper-body plyos and sprinting inside lower-body PLYOS.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: The slot no longer guarantees the movement pattern; weekly volume per bucket is wrong if counted by slot.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Tag every item with its true node (REASSIGN table) and keep a 'cross_listed_in' list so the dropdown behaviour is preserved.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Partly resolved: knee-flexion curls leave AN for RP.LF (COACH-ANSWER CAT-09); dips credited 0.5/0.5 (LIB-16); push press / jerk levels (LIB-13); face pulls pending (LIB-10).

gaps_and_contradictions.title: MID RANGE PUSH exists in the theory tab but not in the library
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: RESISTANCE PATTERNS G6 'MID RANGE PUSH' (incline DB/barbell/cable, viking, landmine); BYOP scatters these into VERTICAL PUSH FOUNDATIONAL (AA9:AA10), HORIZONTAL PUSH ADVANCED (AD91), UL vertical push (AA93); AZ files incline presses under both SHOULDERS/TRAPS and CHEST; 4 TRACKS uses 'HIGH INCLINE PRESS' as a main lift; PPL has an 'Incline' DETAIL slot.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: Incline pressing is credited inconsistently (chest vs delts) and its level is contradictory (foundational seated incline vs advanced incline bench).
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Add RP.PU.M with chest 1.0 / front delts 1.0. Leave RP.PL.M as an open question (no evidence).
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Open (no answer on mid-range push itself). The v0 credit proposal is superseded by VOL-09: until the coach answers, RP.PU.M credits chest 1.0 with front delts and triceps as 0.25 helpers, like bench.

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Core: region conflicts, missing 'BOTH', rigid level = plane
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: Toes to bar / knees to chest: BYOP CT (O15:O16) vs CONTROL PATTERNSCORE CP (I18:I19); V-ups CP vs BOTH; side planks CP vs BOTH; 'Hanging Rotational Knee/Leg Raises' sits in SAGITAL foundational; Sheet23 S (ADVANCED CP TRANSVERSE) empty; BYOP has no 'BOTH' region and no static/dynamic tag; frontal plane nearly empty everywhere.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: A plane-driven core progression will mis-level items and can't produce anti-rotation (static transverse) work at foundational level (e.g. Pallof holds are FN-green).
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Adopt CONTROL PATTERNSCORE's 3-axis grid (region x plane x mode) as the core facets; keep 'plane SAG->FRO->TRA' as the DEFAULT progression, not the definition of level.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Mostly resolved (COACH-ANSWER CAT-08): CT / CP / CB x plane confirmed; toes to bar and Copenhagen plank 'more complicated' (PROPOSED, pending); side planks merged (LIB-17).

gaps_and_contradictions.title: The jumping system is split across two segments and three tracks
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: Ankle/limited-knee track: C124 block (under TRIPPLE EXTENSION) + G44 block (under PLYOS); landing/hurdle track G8 (labelled FOUNDATIONAL) + G89 (labelled MODERATE); G44 (plate hops, limited-knee track) and G89 (hurdles) are two different blocks both labelled MODERATE; FULL JUMPING G124 also holds sprinting and plyo push-ups; MACH drills and acceleration starts exist only in Sheet23; force phases, the Sheet23 plyo 'ZONE 1/2/3' steps (v1: a plyo execution method, not a zone and not an exercise property, CAT-11) and ballistic-vs-plyometric purpose live only in the theory tab.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: The sport dial (basketball more, boxing/karate less, MMA between) has nothing to grip: no field says 'rebounding contact' vs 'landing'.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: One AP.JMP node with three tracks (LK, PLY, FULL) + facets F.PHASE, F.PMETHOD, F.INTENT, F.SSC on every jump item; AP.SPD and AP.UBP as their own nodes.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Resolved for the dials (COACH-ANSWER CAT-10, CAT-11, ATH-01, LIB-21): F.PMETHOD, ground-contact ballistic vs plyometric, AP.SPD confirmed as a category.

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Plane has two meanings and is mostly unfilled for resistance work
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: Theory: plane = direction of the force resisted ('Stance loads the FRONT TO BACK' ...; frontal squat = squat + hip band). Library: every resistance list is sagittal except side lunge / curtsy / lateral step-up; 'lateral step up' filed UNILATERAL SAGITAL; all upper-body FRONTAL/TRANSVERSE blocks empty.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: Athletes who need frontal/transverse resistance (MMA, basketball) cannot be served by plane filtering.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Store plane_of_motion and plane_of_demand separately; populate demand via F.PERTURB and F.LOADLAT (contra/ipsi).
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: The plane definition is still open (no answer). LIB-20 adds frontal / transverse lower-body moves to the library, minus bands and the strap, and UNI-12 (RIGHT) says who gets them: more for basketball, tennis, soccer and MMA, little for aesthetics clients.

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Laterality vocabulary is overloaded
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: 'BILATERAL SYMMETRICAL' (upper) vs 'BILATERAL' (lower); 'UNILATERAL' is both a laterality (row 5) and a level block (U89, X89, AA89, AD124); staggered stance with two-hand load is 'BILATERAL LOADING' under UNILATERAL SAGITAL; alternating/offset only in names; load laterality (contra/ipsi) separate from stance laterality.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: Filters on 'unilateral' return the wrong sets.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Resolved (COACH-ANSWER CAT-13, UNI-07): load laterality semantics and use cases; alternating = unilateral.

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Muscle tags disagree between library and program, and several muscles have no home
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: 'SHOULDERS/TRAPS' (AA6) vs slot 'Chest/Shoulders'; 'SHOULDERS' (AH6) vs 'Shoulders/Traps'; 'GLUTES/HAMSTRINGS' (AN6) vs slot 'Hamstring'; dips chest (PPL) vs triceps (AZ); incline chest vs shoulders (AZ); hip thrusts glutes vs hamstrings (AZ); no rear-delt slot outside PPL; no adductors, abductors, erectors, forearms, neck, rotator cuff.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: 15-20 sets/muscle accounting is impossible to reproduce exactly.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Canonical muscle list (MUSCLES) with credit weights per node; keep coach labels as aliases.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Partly resolved (COACH-ANSWER CAT-02, LIB-16, VOL-17): big/small lists, dips credit, rear delts get own sets; front delts, traps, adductors, neck still unclassified.

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Conditioning has two taxonomies that do not meet
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: Library CARDIO sub-blocks (SPEED INTERVALS, DISTANCE ..., CALORIES) carry no A/B/C colour; the AEROBIC cheat sheet (A/B/C + lactate clearance) has no library; BASEBALL uses energy zones (SPEED ENDURANCE / SPEED POWER / SPEED STRENGTH & POWER) and 'Buy out'; CrossFit uses WODs and levels; cheat sheet asks 3 sessions/week, athletic templates give 2; DISTANCE and CALORIES blocks unreachable from B7:B122.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: The generator cannot satisfy 'one of each colour per week' from library picks.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Tag every CA item with F.ABAND and F.EZONE; treat formats as F.CFORMAT.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Open in the taxonomy (A/B/C tags); 3 / 2 / 4 aerobic sessions per week by population is a profile rule (ATH-07). The cardio dropdowns are to be extended so the DISTANCE (200-1000 m) and CALORIES blocks can be picked, 'just make sure they're logical' (COACH-ANSWER FIX-02); any colour can run on any erg, tracked by calories, time or distance (EQ-14).

gaps_and_contradictions.title: FUNCTIONAL layer, carries and drags are skeletons with no slot
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: Only ANTERIOR OBLIQUE SYSTEM has items (17); POSTERIOR OBLIQUE / LATERAL SUBSYSTEM / CARRY / DRAGS are headers only; none is wired to any program tab; 'single side carry' is filed as CORE THORAX TRANSVERSE DYNAMIC in CONTROL PATTERNSCORE.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: These ideas cannot reach a client today.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Keep as nodes (FN.*) with status 'unpopulated'; allow them to fill CO and X.PREP slots once populated.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Build-out confirmed (COACH-ANSWER LIB-19): carries and drags for athletes and general fitness; slings for advanced athletes and rehab.

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Throwing and COD are levelled differently from everything else
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: THROWING: 'AP - THROWING' (no level), ordered by biomechanical complexity, sides always R/L; SPECIALTIES and CORE EXTRAS not in BYOP. COD: football receiver routes graded by turn; agility (reactive) defined but empty; formations undefined.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: COD for non-football athletes and throw progression need rules.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: AP.THR children by description grammar; F.HIPDIR/F.LOADLAT; AP.COD with F.TURN; AP.AGI unpopulated.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Resolved (COACH-ANSWER LIB-06, ATH-06, LIB-01): throws have no levels; COD routes for every athlete by turn angle; L-test and 5-10-5 decoded.

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Program slot grammars are all different
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: BYOP PURPOSE/CATEGORY ('Quads'/'Bilateral KD'), PPL DETAIL ('Incline','Flies','Dips','Push','Overhead','Reverse Flies'), BASEBALL codes ('bkd','uhd','horiz pull', Part A-E), CrossFit ('KNEE DOM','HIP DOM','LB','UB'), 4 TRACKS roles ('the work' ... 'the survival'), HYBRID ('UNI HD','OLY/ POWER','A/C', 'KD' on deadlifts), gym templates (no labels at all).
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: There is no single slot vocabulary to generate into.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Everything crosswalks to node IDs (sec. 6) plus F.ROLE for session position.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Unchanged (crosswalk to node ids + F.ROLE); slot roles confirmed (ORD-07).

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Spelling, spacing and copy drift
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: 'TRIPPLE', 'DOMNANT', 'INTERMIDIATE', 'FOUNDATINONAL', 'SAGITAL', 'UNLATERAL', 'UNILARTERAL', 'ABdution', 'Harmstring', 'Back ' vs 'Back', 'FOUNDATIONAL  ', 'UNILATERAL  ', 'EASY  ', 'CHOSE 👇', date-corrupted '5-10-5'; three library copies disagree (Machine bench press, Barbell Incline Bench Press, SPEED ENDURANCE TEST, truncated plyos).
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: Normalise with strip()/case-fold and the crosswalk; never edit the coach's sheets.
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Resolved (COACH-ANSWER FIX-04): correct spelling in the generator, never in the sheets.

gaps_and_contradictions.title: Equipment / constraint is a coach axis with no field
gaps_and_contradictions.evidence: CHAT-relayed: 'If you read the workouts you can understand them by their equipment usage'; machines = constraints/safer/volume; free weights = skill. Library has no equipment column; NO ACCESS tabs use the full gym lists.
gaps_and_contradictions.impact: Home/no-gym clients and injured/older clients cannot be filtered.
gaps_and_contradictions.proposal: F.IMPL + F.CONSTRAINT on every record (sibling equipment analysis already scores them).
gaps_and_contradictions.v1_status: Resolved (COACH-ANSWER EQ-13, EQ-11, EQ-01): approved 1-5 constraint scale; machines not ranked; no bands; F.AXIAL added (PER-04).

principles: Keep the coach's two-level slot logic: PURPOSE (muscle/quality credited) x CATEGORY (pattern bucket). Do not replace it with a muscle-only or exercise-only model.
Keep his families and codes (AP, RP, CT/CP, BS, UL) and his level words in the UI; use the canonical IDs underneath.
One meaning per field. Level, plyo execution method, Davidson position zone, aerobic band, energy zone, plane of motion, plane of demand, stance laterality and load laterality are separate fields.
An exercise lives in exactly one canonical node; dropdown behaviour is preserved with a 'cross_listed_in' list.

Base exercise + variables (his 'Box *ANY Squat ...' grammar) instead of a flat list wherever he already listed variables (lunges, squats, hinges, presses). Variables are the block-to-block lever: exercises stay fixed for a 4-6 week block, and the next block changes one or two of grip, stance, implement, ROM or rep range, never all at once (COACH-ANSWER PER-02).

Nothing is deleted from the sheets' record: unfinished buckets (FN.*, AP.AGI, RP.PU.M, RP.PL.M) stay as nodes marked 'unpopulated'/'proposed'; removed or dormant items (strap, Camporini, bands, chains, weight releasers) stay in the archive with a status.
Biomechanics describes every exercise; it is not a bucket (COACH-ANSWER CAT-03).
Every exercise carries every lens at once so the generator can segment by any of them (COACH-ANSWER CAT-01).
Levels are soft defaults that add options and never lock exercises (COACH-ANSWER CAT-05).
No bands and no variable resistance for now: F.ACCOM is a dormant axis (COACH-ANSWER EQ-01, EQ-12).

science.reference: Israetel M, Davis M, Feather J, Hoffmann J - Scientific Principles of Hypertrophy Training (Renaissance Periodization, 2021)
science.relevance: Muscle-specific volume landmarks (MV, MEV, MAV, MRV), weekly sets per muscle, set progression across a mesocycle then deload, stimulus-to-fatigue ratio (SFR). Basis for counting sets per MUSCLE and for small muscles tolerating more sets/frequency.

science.reference: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW (2017) J Sports Sci 35(11):1073-1082 - dose-response of weekly sets and hypertrophy
science.relevance: Graded dose-response; >=10 sets/muscle/week produced more growth than <5 or 5-9. Consistent with (but does not by itself establish) the coach's 15-20 sets/muscle/week target - the meta-analysis did not test 15-20 as a separate band.

science.reference: Baz-Valle E et al. (2022) J Hum Kinet 81:199-210 - training volume and hypertrophy
science.relevance: Suggests ~12-20 weekly sets per muscle as a practical range for trained people.

science.reference: Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J, Van Every DW, Plotkin DL (2021) Sports 9(2):32 - the repetition continuum re-examined
science.relevance: Hypertrophy is similar across a wide load range (roughly 6-30+ reps) when sets are taken close to failure. Supports 'everyone picks between 5 and 30 reps' and higher reps for isolation/small muscles.

science.reference: Refalo MC et al. (2023) Sports Med 53:649-665 - proximity to failure and hypertrophy
science.relevance: Sets need to end reasonably close to failure; supports the coach's 1-3 RIR rule and the EFFORT '8 - That was perfect' bullseye.

science.reference: Zourdos MC et al. (2016) JSCR 30(1):267-275; Helms ER et al. (2016) SCJ 38(4):42-49 - RIR-based RPE
science.relevance: RPE 10 = 0 RIR, 9 = 1 RIR, 8 = 2 RIR, 7 = 3 RIR. On this scale the coach's 'HYPERTROPHY FOCUSED WORKOUTS (1 RIR) *RPE8+' is loose (1 RIR = RPE 9), while '1-3 RIR ... aka RPE 7+' (UL/PPL A6) matches. Keep his labels verbatim; the generator should store RIR as the primary field.

science.reference: Davidson P - Rethinking the Big Patterns (RTBP) course and the book 'A Coach's Guide to Optimizing Movement' (the coach's named source for the zones, COACH-ANSWER CAT-04 / CAT-10)
science.relevance: Movement understood through positions, reference points/constraints, relative pelvis-thorax motion, hip internal/external rotation ('into'/'out of' a hip) and planes; load position and stance change the demand. Basis for bucketing big movements and athletic work by BIOMECHANICS rather than muscle. v1: the coach's zones (vertical = external-rotation bias; horizontal zone 2 = internal-rotation bias, compressive) are attributed to this book; the zone wording was not found in public summaries, so it rests on the coach's account (F.DZONE).

science.reference: Contreras B, Cronin J, Schoenfeld BJ et al. (2013) SCJ 35(2):17-22 - force vectors in hip-extension exercises
science.relevance: Exercises classified by the direction of the load vector relative to the body; parallels the coach's reading of plane as the direction of the force resisted.
Anti-extension / anti-lateral-flexion / anti-rotation ('static') vs flexion/rotation ('dynamic') - parallels CONTROL PATTERNSCORE's STATIC/DYNAMIC x plane grid.

science.reference: Vleeming A et al. (1995) Spine 20(7):753-758; Lee D - The Pelvic Girdle (myofascial slings)
science.relevance: Anterior oblique, posterior oblique and lateral subsystems - the FUNCTIONAL BIOMECHANICS SYSTEM columns.

science.reference: Flanagan EP, Comyns TM (2008) SCJ 30(5):32-38 - fast SSC and reactive strength index
science.relevance: Fast SSC (<250 ms contacts) vs slow SSC; parallels 'PLYOMETRIC PURPOSE - BE REACTIVE & BOUNCY' vs 'BALLISTIC PURPOSE - BE EXPLOSIVELY & FAST' and the SSC speed tiers. v1: grounds the coach's ground-contact rule (COACH-ANSWER ATH-01, CAT-10): long contact = ballistic, short contact = plyometric.

science.reference: Dietz C, Peterson B (2012) Triphasic Training
science.relevance: Triphasic = eccentric -> isometric -> concentric blocks (a reactive/peaking block follows), plus French contrast. The coach's 'TAKING IN FORCES -> DELIVER FORCES FAST -> AMORTIZATION -> REBOUNDING' is a loose parallel (his order is not the same sequence), and 'FRENCH CONTRAST' (ALL ABOUT SQUATS G16) is an outside model he has absorbed.

science.reference: Suchomel TJ, Comfort P, Stone MH (2015) Sports Med 45(6):823-839 - weightlifting pulling derivatives
science.relevance: Pulls from the hang as foundational, catch variations later; matches the TRIPPLE EXTENSION ladder.

science.reference: Sheppard JM, Young WB (2006) J Sports Sci 24(9):919-932 - agility classification
science.relevance: Pre-planned change of direction vs reactive agility - the coach's 'COD: Proactive' vs 'Agility: Reactive' definitions.

science.reference: Seiler S (2010) IJSPP 5(3):276-291 - intensity distribution in endurance training
science.relevance: Intensity zones distributed across the week. CAUTION: Seiler's evidence favours a POLARISED distribution (~80% of sessions/time at low intensity, little at moderate). The coach's rule (AEROBIC A5: one blue, one green, one orange session per week, 3 total) is an even 1:1:1 session split, so it parallels the idea of zones, not Seiler's distribution.

Size principle: motor units are recruited small-to-large as force demand rises, so heavier loads recruit more high-threshold units - supports 'HEAVY BARBELL' (ALL ABOUT SQUATS A44). The coach's 'ECCENTRIC SLOW MORE MUSCLE RECRUITMENTS' / 'ECCENTRICFAST LESS MUSCLE RECRUITMENT' (A45/A48) is his own tempo claim, not part of the size principle (with light loads, going faster or closer to failure also raises recruitment).

science.reference: Stastny P et al. (2015) J Strength Cond Res 29(11):3177-3187 - dumbbell-carrying position in split squats and walking lunges
science.relevance: Contralateral loading raised gluteus medius activity in the dynamic forward lunge but not in the static split squat. Supports the coach's contralateral 'into the hip' use for change-of-direction athletes (CAT-13); via 07_science_lineage.md [P4].

science.reference: Postural Restoration Institute / Bill Hartman / Pat Davidson pressure model (expansion vs compression; via 07_science_lineage.md [P1][D10])
science.relevance: Expansion ~ external rotation, compression ~ internal rotation. The closest public parallel to the coach's zone rotation bias (CAT-10); practitioner model, not peer-reviewed evidence.
